annotations.text:
THE SURFACE

Web-first: stoke serves this page itself on 127.0.0.1:8080, inside the one static binary Phase 1 already requires. No Electron, no installer, no code signing, and you can watch the swarm from your phone while the box works.

A Tauri shell can wrap this exact page later for tray, folder-picker and auto-start — same frontend, no rewrite. That is the only thing the desktop path adds, and it costs Windows signing and SmartScreen reputation, so it waits until there are users.

DIRECTION A — INSTRUMENT

Dense and dark. Lanes, block map, scheduler and residency all on one screen, nothing folded away. Reads like htop for inference: you lean in and everything is already there.

Tradeoff: it asks you to lean in. Nothing on it is legible from across the room, and it is the busiest of the three.

DIRECTION B — CONTROL ROOM · CHOSEN, SECOND PASS

Rebuilt for a professional read. Gone: the vertical side-rail text, the 104px display number, the airy 0.3em letterspacing, the ragged agent rows.

In: a real column grid with headers and tabular numerals, section tabs where a console expects them, a four-up KPI strip on hairlines, TTFT p50/p99 next to throughput, a status bar with session and build, and the per-block pool view brought back — its absence was this direction's one real weakness.

Colour is now carried by one tamed accent (chroma 0.09, not 0.13) doing state duty only, with the shared prefix in a muted blue that never competes with it.

DIRECTION C — BLUEPRINT

Light, technical-drawing language: hairlines, figure numbers, dimension callouts, graph-paper ground. This is the direction that screenshots into the README and the design notes without looking like a toy.

Tradeoff: white light at 2am is the wrong instrument for a box doing overnight work, and it feels the least live of the three.

Whichever direction wins, this view is the argument for the product — so it is drawn once, properly, here.

The numbers are the engine's own: 16 tokens per block (BP_BLOCK_TOKENS), 36 layers, 147 KB of KV per token at f16, blocks shared by refcount and given back under memory pressure.
